nyiso.Project Name: U-21 and V-22 ACR Line Reconductoring
nyiso.Description: The U-21 and V-22 lines have poletop and cross arm decay as well as woodpecker damage along the entire length of the lines. Lines have experienced tree contacts and lightning strikes requiring addition of shield wire. Solution: Rebuild U21 and V22 lines to 115kV standards. Replace all 594 wood structures with 115 kV standard steel structures, reconductor both U-21 and V-22 lines and install OPGW. Alternative 1: Full re-build of both lines to 69kV standards, all structures would be removed and replaced with steel, OPGW installed. This option is expected to cost 4% less than the proposed solution, it will not be able to address future load growth in the area and increased capacity per the 2050 Load Study. Alternative 2: Only replace the structures that need immediate replacement (Rolling replacement). This option was not selected as this would put significant risk on reliability of the line with an increasing rate of wood structure asset damage year-over-year. The duration and cost would be negatively impacted this approach. Alternative 3: Full re-build of both lines to 115kV standards with advanced conductors. Composite/carbon core conductors did not reduce structure heights/quantities adding to project cost.

pjm.Description: Rebuild and reconductor 2.9 miles of overhead transmission line from the Chesterfield Substation to just south of the Tyler Substation in Chesterfield County, Virginia. The operating voltage will remain 230 kV while new structures and higher-capacity conductors replace aging infrastructure, increase ampacity, and support regional data center growth, local generation, and reliability needs through Dominion Energy's supplemental transmission planning process.

The project directly connects PSE&G's Kilmer substation and Lake Nelson substation. Because the lines sit within or interface with PSE&G's territory, PSE&G is responsible for executing the inside-plant modifications, line drops, and terminal equipment upgrades at these stations. The New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (NJBPU) is the governing state agency funding and driving this grid expansion. They requested these upgrades under PJM's State Agreement Approach to successfully inject 6,400 MW of offshore wind energy into the regional electric grid

spp.Project Name: WAPA Shasta-Keswick 230 kV transmission line reconductoring with 795-T16 ACCR
spp.Description: WAPA reconductored the Shasta and Keswick substations and the associated 230 kV transmission facilities with 795-T16 ACCR conductor during 2013-2014. The work addressed N-2 overload risk: loss of both Shasta-Cottonwood 230 kV lines could overload the Shasta-Keswick 230 kV line. The ACCR conductor provides over 2,000 amps, allowing each bay to carry the full 710 MW output of the Shasta power plant. The diameter-equivalent conductor met the existing sag without increasing tension and avoided major structure replacement. ACCR was used for jack-bus and drop-down jumpers; 1590 AAC connected the high-temperature strain bus to terminals not rated for high-temperature operation.
